Physics (PHY)

PHY 301  Mechanics  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Designed for students who intend to major in science or mathematics. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 303, Physics 301, 302K, 303K, 309K, 317K. Three lecture hours and one small-group discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Mathematics 408D, 408L, or 408S, and Physics 101L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 101L  Laboratory for Physics 301  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 101L, 102M, 103M, 105M, 117M. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 301.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 302K  General Physics Technical Course: Mechanics, Heat, and Sound  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 1301)  
3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Noncalculus technical course in physics. Completion of high school trigonometry or Mathematics 305G is highly recommended. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 303, Physics 301, 302K, 303K, 309K, 317K. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 102M or 105M.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 302L  General Physics Technical Course: Electricity and Magnetism, Light, Atomic and Nuclear Physics  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 1302)  
3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Noncalculus technical course in physics. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 304, Physics 302L, 303L, 309L, 316, 317L. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 302K and 102M or 105M with a grade of at least C-; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Physics 102N or 105N.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 102M  Laboratory for Physics 302K  1 Hour  

(TCCN: PHYS 1101)  
0 Lecture Hours  2 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 101L, 102M, 103M, 105M, 117M. Two laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 302K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 102N  Laboratory for Physics 302L  1 Hour  

(TCCN: PHYS 1102)  
0 Lecture Hours  2 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 102N, 103N, 105N, 116L, 117N. Two laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 302L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 303E  Electromagnetic, Quantum, and Semiconductor Physics  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Discuss electricity, magnetism, electromagnetic waves, photons, matter waves, atomic physics, band structure, semiconductors, diodes, and transistors. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Electrical and Computer Engineering 302 (or Electrical Engineering 302) or Electrical and Computer Engineering 302H (or Electrical Engineering 302H), Physics 303K and 103M or 105M with a grade of at least C- in each; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Math 408D or 408M.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 303K  Engineering Physics I  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 2325)  
4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
A general survey of physics; primarily laws of motion, heat, and wave phenomena. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 303, Physics 301, 302K, 303K, 309K, 317K. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Mathematics 408D, 408L, or 408S, and Physics 103M or 105M.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 303L  Engineering Physics II  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 2326)  
4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Electricity and magnetism, optics, and atomic phenomena. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 304, Physics 302L, 303L, 309L, 316, 317L. Three lecture hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 303K and 103M or 105M with a grade of at least C- in each; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Mathematics 408D or 408M, and Physics 103N or 105N.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 103M  Laboratory for Physics 303K  1 Hour  

(TCCN: PHYS 2125)  
0 Lecture Hours  2 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 101L, 102M, 103M, 105M, 117M. Two laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 303K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 103N  Laboratory for Physics 303L  1 Hour  

(TCCN: PHYS 2126)  
1 Lecture Hours  2 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 102N, 103N, 105N, 116L, 117N. Two laboratory hours and one discussion hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 303L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 104  Introductory Physics Seminar  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Discussion of the development of important ideas in physics, with emphasis on their relevance to contemporary research. One lecture hour a week for one semester.
Restrictions: Suggested for beginning physics majors.  
Grading: Pass/Fail  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 105M  Laboratory For Physics 302K, 303K, and 317K  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Participate in an introductory mechanics laboratory. Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 101L, 102M, 103M, 105M, 117M. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 302K, 303K, or 317K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 105N  Laboratory For Physics 302L, 303L, and 317L  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Participate in an introductory electricity, magnetism, and optics laboratory. Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 102N, 103N, 105N, 116L, 117N. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 302L, 303L or 317L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 306  Elementary Physics Methods  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Designed for students who have not had high school physics, have weak problem-solving skills, and need preparation for Physics 301 or 303K. May not be counted toward any degree. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: High school trigonometry or Mathematics 305G.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 108  Introduction to Research  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introductory laboratory experience; use of tools and test equipment; beginning apprenticeship in active physics research. One class hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Consent of instructor and approval of an undergraduate adviser.  
Grading: Pass/Fail  
Repeatable for credit: Yes (Unlimited)  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 208F, 308F  Introduction to Research  2-3 Hours  

2,3 Lecture Hours  3,4.5 Lab Hours  
Introductory laboratory experience; use of tools and test equipment; beginning apprenticeship in active physics research. For each semester hour of credit earned, the equivalent of one lecture hour and one and a half laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Consent of instructor and the undergraduate adviser.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 309K  Elementary Physics for Nontechnical Students  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 1305)  
3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Mechanics, heat, and sound. Designed for students who do not intend to do further work in natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, or medicine. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 303, Physics 301, 302K, 303K, 309K, 317K. May not be counted toward a degree in the College of Natural Sciences. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 309L  Elementary Physics for Nontechnical Students  3 Hours  

(TCCN: PHYS 1307)  
3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Electricity and magnetism, light, atomic and nuclear physics. Designed for students who do not intend to do further work in natural sciences, engineering, mathematics, or medicine. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 304, Physics 302L, 303L, 309L, 316, 317L. May not be counted toward a degree in the College of Natural Sciences. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 309K with a grade of at least C-.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 110, 210, 310, 410, 510, 610, 710, 810, 910  Topics in Physics  1-9 Hours  

1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
For each semester hour of credit earned, the equivalent of one lecture hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Varies with the topic.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 110C  Topics in Conference Course  1 Hour  

1 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Supervised study of selected topics in physics, by individual arrangement with department and instructor. Conference course.
Pre/Corequisites: Written consent of instructor.  
Grading: Pass/Fail  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 315  Wave Motion and Optics  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Study of general properties of waves; examples include sound, electromagnetic, and mechanical waves; special emphasis on light and optics. Three lecture hours and one small-group discussion hour a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 316 and 116L with a grade of at least C- in each; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Mathematics 427J or 427K, and Physics 115L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 115L  Laboratory for Physics 315  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
May not be counted toward a degree unless prerequisite is observed. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 315.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 316  Electricity and Magnetism  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 304, Physics 302L, 303L, 309L, 316, 317L. Three lecture hours and one small-group discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 301 and 101L with a grade of at least C- in each; credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Mathematics 408D or 408M, and Physics 116L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 116L  Laboratory for Physics 316  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 102N, 103N, 105N, 116L, 117N. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 316.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 317K  General Physics I  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Mechanics, heat, and sound, with biomedical applications. An introductory course designed and recommended primarily for premedical students and others in the biomedical sciences whose professional or preprofessional training includes an introductory course in calculus. Satisfies most medical and dental school requirements for physics. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 303, Physics 301, 302K, 303K, 309K, 317K. May not be counted toward the Bachelor of Science in Astronomy or Bachelor of Science in Physics. Three lecture hours and one small-group discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- in Mathematics 408C or 408R; or credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Mathematics 408L or 408S; and credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 117M or 105M.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 317L  General Physics II  3 Hours  

4 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Electricity and magnetism, light, atomic and molecular physics, nuclear physics, and their biomedical applications. Designed and recommended primarily for premedical students and others in the biomedical sciences whose professional or preprofessional training includes an introductory course in calculus. Satisfies most medical and dental school requirements for physics. Only one of the following may be counted: Physical Science 304, Physics 302L, 303L, 309L, 316, 317L. May not be counted toward the Bachelor of Science in Astronomy or Bachelor of Science in Physics. Three lecture hours and one small-group discussion hour a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Physics 317K and 117M or 105M with a grade of at least C-; and credit with a grade of at least C- or registration in Physics 117N or 105N.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 117M  Laboratory for Physics 317K  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 101L, 102M, 103M, 105M, 117M. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 317K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 117N  Laboratory for Physics 317L  1 Hour  

0 Lecture Hours  3 Lab Hours  
Only one of the following may be counted: Physics 102N, 103N, 105N, 116L, 117N. Three laboratory hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Physics 317L.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Lower Division  

PHY 119S, 219S, 319S, 419S, 519S, 619S, 719S, 819S, 919S  Topics in Physics  1-9 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
This course is used to record credit the student earns while enrolled at another institution in a program administered by the University's Study Abroad Office. Credit is recorded as assigned by the study abroad adviser in the Department of Physics. University credit is awarded for work in an exchange program; it may be counted as coursework taken in residence. Transfer credit is awarded for work in an affiliated studies program.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  

PHY 321  Modern Physics: Plan II  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Conceptual foundations of modern physics. Examines quantum mechanics, quantum field theory, relativity, and general relativity, including large-scale structure and cosmology; and the development of analytic problem-solving skills, including estimation. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Core Curriculum: 030  
Pre/Corequisites: Upper-division standing.  
Restrictions: Restricted to Plan II students.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

PHY 329  Introduction to Computational Physics  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Computational methods for problem solving and research in physics; numerical analysis and computer simulation methods for physics applications using different types of computers. Only one of the following may be counted: Computer Science 367, Mathematics 368K, Physics 329. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: The following coursework with a grade of at least C- in each: Physics 315 and 115L; a programming course at the level of Computer Science 303E with a grade of at least C- and credit with a grade of at least C- or registration for Mathematics 340L, 341, or Statistics and Data Sciences 329C.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Upper Division  

PHY 129S, 229S, 329S, 429S, 529S, 629S, 729S, 829S, 929S  Topics in Physics  1-9 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
This course is used to record credit the student earns while enrolled at another institution in a program administered by the University's Study Abroad Office. Credit is recorded as assigned by the study abroad adviser in the Department of Physics. University credit is awarded for work in an exchange program; it may be counted as coursework taken in residence. Transfer credit is awarded for work in an affiliated studies program.
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  

PHY 329W  Cooperative Physics  3 Hours  

0 Lecture Hours  40 Lab Hours  
Covers the work period of physics students in the Cooperative Education Program, which provides supervised work experience by arrangement with the employer and the supervising instructor. The student must repeat the course each work period and must take it twice to receive credit toward the degree; at least one of these registrations must be during a fall or spring semester. No more than three semester hours may be counted toward the major requirement; no more than six semester hours may be counted toward the degree. The student's first registration must be on the pass/fail basis. Forty laboratory hours a week for one semester.

PHY 341  Selected Topics in Physics  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours

Pre/Corequisites: Upper-division standing, three semester hours of coursework in a natural science, and three semester hours of coursework in mathematics.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: May be repeated for credit when the topics vary.  
Academic Level: Upper Division  
Topic 1: Energy Production. The various means that exist or have been suggested for generating energy; comparison in terms of efficiency, safety, and effects on the environment.

Topic 2: Great Men, Moments, and Ideas. How our views of matter, energy, and the universe developed.

Topic 3: Musical Acoustics. Study of the production, transmission, and perception of the special kind of sound called music, based on the application of elementary principles of physics.

Topic 4: The Nature of Things. A qualitative survey of all of physics, from falling bodies to quarks, making heavy use of classroom demonstrations.

Topic 5: Pseudoscience. Study of a variety of ideas treated very seriously by the communications media but having no basis in fact, including astrology, extrasensory perception, and flying saucers; why such areas are not part of science.

Topic 6: Writing.

Topic 7: Research Methods: UTeach.

Examine the foundational principles and cutting-edge applications of advanced optical spectroscopy methods. Analyze the electrodynamics of solids (metals, insulators, semiconductors), which exhibit complex and rich electromagnetic behavior. Study the key components of a basic optical spectroscopy setup. Explore advanced spectroscopy techniques and current research frontiers in the field. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing. For undergraduate students: Physics 315, 373, 375S, or consent of instructor and graduate advisor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 392Q  Density Functional Theory  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Examine the quantum theory of many-electron systems from the point of view of first-principles atomic-scale calculations. Develop the conceptual foundations of density functional theory and its uses in computational materials modeling, design, and discovery. Perform predictive calculations of structural, electronic, optical, vibrational, and magnetic properties of solids using high-performance computing environments. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral

PHY 395K  Nonlinear Optics and Lasers  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Gaussian beam optics, interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter, semiclassical laser theory, experimental laser systems, nonlinear optical susceptibilities, harmonic generation, wave mixing, electro-optic and acousto-optic effects, coherent transient effects, optical breakdown, laser-plasma interactions. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, and either Physics 387K and 389K or consent of instructor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 395M  Laser Physics  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Continuation of Physics 395K. Advanced atomic physics of various laser systems, optical coherence and diffraction theory, pulse propagation and dispersion effects, advanced laser oscillator and amplifier physics, laser amplifier chain design, and chirped-pulse amplification. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, Physics 387K, 389K, and 395K, and consent of instructor.  
Grading: Student Option

PHY 396G  Cosmology  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Explore inflationary cosmology, the formation of element abundances during Big Bang nucleosynthesis, cosmological perturbations and structure formation, the cosmic microwave background, and the content of the universe (including dark matter and dark energy). Examine unresolved problems in cosmology (such as the origin of the matter/antimatter asymmetry), the possibility of extra dimensions, what happened before the Big Bang, "big data" in cosmology, observational probes of dark energy, and inflation models and tests. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, Physics 389K, and consent of instructor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 396J  Introduction to Elementary Particle Physics  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Historical introduction to elementary particles, elementary particle dynamics, relativistic kinematics, symmetries, bound states, the Feynman calculus, quantum electrodynamics, electrodynamics of quarks and hadrons, quantum chromodynamics, weak interactions, gauge theories. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, Physics 389K, and knowledge of special relativity and scattering.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 396K  Quantum Field Theory I  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Quantization of the Klein-Gordon, Dirac, and electromagnetic field theories; theory of interacting fields, perturbation theory, and renormalization. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing and Physics 389K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 396L  Quantum Field Theory II  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Path-integral formalism, massless particles, electrodynamics, nonperturbative methods, one-loop calculations in quantum electrodynamics, general renormalization theory, soft photons, bound statics in quantum electrodynamics. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing and Physics 396K.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral  

PHY 396P  String Theory I  3 Hours  

3 Lecture Hours  0 Lab Hours  
Introduction to string theory and conformal field theory. The free string, conformal invariance and conformal field theory, supersymmetry and string interactions. Three lecture hours a week for one semester.
Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing, and Physics 396K or the equivalent or consent of instructor.  
Grading: Student Option  
Repeatable for credit: No  
Academic Level: Doctoral

Pre/Corequisites: Graduate standing and Physics 396P.  
Grading: Student Option
